summary.intent: Capture implementation decisions for Phase 67 (TEE Lease-Renewer Contract Rewrite) by scouting the existing TEE worker code and spec, discussing gray areas with the user, and producing a CONTEXT.md to guide downstream research and planning agents.
summary.outcome: All four gray areas resolved and locked; 67-CONTEXT.md and 67-DISCUSSION-LOG.md written and committed to feat/tee-lease-renewer-contract-rewrite; 18 load-bearing code/spec claims adversarially verified against the live tree before commit.

repo: Current TEE worker is the INVERSE of the target contract: it ORIGINATES a fresh IPNS record from relay-supplied scalars (entry.latestCid + sequenceNumber+1n) rather than parsing/verifying an incoming marshaled record.

Signing inputs for TEE come entirely from ipns_republish_schedule rows (via getDueEntries/scheduleRepository), never from canonical ipns_records — ipns_records is only written back on success via syncIpnsRecordSequence.
The write-back in syncIpnsRecordSequence uses LessThanOrEqual(newSequenceNumber), NOT an equality CAS — a weaker guard than the Phase-66 client publish CAS in IpnsService.upsertIpnsRecord.

The only existing tombstone guard (tombstonedAt: IsNull() in syncIpnsRecordSequence) runs AFTER delegated-routing publish — it blocks DB sequence resurrection but not the TEE signing or IPNS publish itself, requiring a pre-publish gate.

No name-to-key binding exists anywhere in apps/tee-worker/src — the handler decrypts the IPNS private key, signs entry.latestCid for entry.ipnsName, and never asserts publicKeyFromIpnsName(ipnsName) == pubkey(decryptedKey).

Local docker-compose.yml does NOT run the tee-worker; it only runs in staging (docker-compose.staging.yml) and production CVM configs — so adding the worker to local compose is a required Phase 67 task.

Republish is a BullMQ queue processor; getDueEntries selects WHERE nextRepublishAt <= now(), so an e2e test can own its own scheduling by writing nextRepublishAt to the past + enqueuing one explicit job — no cron wait needed.

ipns_republish_schedule has 4 columns duplicating ipns_records state: encrypted_ipns_key (vs encrypted_ipns_private_key), key_epoch, latest_cid, sequence_number. The encrypted-key duplicate uses a DIFFERENT column name per table.

TEE unit tests (Vitest, republish.test.ts) mock the IPNS signer via vi.mock('../services/ipns-signer.js'), so actual record marshaling/EOL/signature are not exercised. Relay-side specs fully mock TeeService.republish. No TEE round-trip E2E exists.
Simulator mode is the default (TEE_MODE || 'simulator'); production uses Phala DstackClient.getKey for epoch-keyed ECIES key derivation.

Phase-66 atomic CAS (WHERE sequenceNumber = :expected AND generation <= :incoming AND tombstoned_at IS NULL) lives in IpnsService.upsertIpnsRecord (client publish path only), not touched by the TEE renewal path.

code.finding: Sequence increment (+1n) and fresh record origination from relay-supplied scalars — the exact lines the rewrite must change to same-seq, same-CID, later-EOL-only.
TEE_RECORD_LIFETIME_MS = 48 * 60 * 60 * 1000 — hardcoded EOL, no extend-existing-record path.
teeEntries map builds TEE request from schedule batch entry (schedule rows), never reads ipns_records to construct signing inputs.
syncIpnsRecordSequence write-back uses LessThanOrEqual(newSequenceNumber) — forward-only, not an equality CAS; also tombstonedAt: IsNull() guard here runs post-publish.
Phase-66 atomic CAS with equality sequenceNumber + generation <= + tombstoned_at IS NULL lives here (client publish path), with 409/410 disambiguation — TEE renewal does NOT go through this path.
Four duplicated columns: encrypted_ipns_key (:39-40), key_epoch (:46-47), latest_cid (:52-53), sequence_number (:59-60) — all collapse into ipns_records in Phase 67.
vi.mock('../services/ipns-signer.js') means the IPNS signer is mocked in all unit tests — real record marshaling/seq/EOL assertions are untested at the unit level.

workflow: GSD discuss-phase workflow: scout codebase in parallel with loading prior context, then present gray areas, discuss each, adversarially verify all load-bearing claims before writing CONTEXT.md.
Running a verification workflow (parallel adversarial agents) on scout-reported facts before baking them into a CONTEXT.md prevents compounding errors from single-source trust.
BullMQ-based background jobs can be driven deterministically in e2e tests by combining a direct DB row update (set nextRepublishAt to past) with an explicit queue.add() call — no cron dependency.
Phase branch naming: feat/<phase-slug>; first commit pattern: docs(NN): capture phase context.
gsd_run commit reports commit_failed but the commit actually lands — known false-negative from lint-staged progress detection; verify with git log rather than retrying.

friction: gsd_run commit false-negative: helper reports commit_failed even when the commit succeeds, requiring a manual git log verification step after every commit.
